episode_title: Ep. 39: CTV, Walled Gardens & the Future of Open Web Monetization

real_qa.q: What percentage of open web impression share has declined over recent years according to Xplain measurements?
real_qa.r: According to Xplain data, open web dropped by 10 points in terms of share of impressions measured across their aggregated client base over the last couple of years. While Fabien emphasizes this is anecdotal rather than statistically significant, it shows year-over-year decline in the open web's share of digital media plans.
real_qa.requete: open web impression share decline Xplain

real_qa.q: Why does Xplain recommend premium publishers use attention-based KPIs instead of completion and viewability metrics?
real_qa.r: Fabien explains that completion and viewability metrics fail to capture the true quality premium publishers deliver. Attention-based KPIs that measure ad clutter, share of screen, time in view, sound rate, and quality of context create a multifactorial definition of quality. This allows premium publishers to objectively demonstrate their value to brands and differentiate from non-premium publishers, whereas traditional metrics treat all impressions equally.
real_qa.requete: attention metrics vs viewability premium publishers

real_qa.q: What are the main flaws in post-click and post-view attribution models that advertisers commonly use?
real_qa.r: Post-click attribution favors users most likely to convert, incentivizing retargeting of users already about to purchase rather than acquiring new customers. Post-view attribution is even worse, encouraging sellers to ignore impression quality entirely and focus on cookie-bombing users with unseen or non-viewable impressions just to get credited for the last touch before a conversion, regardless of whether the impression actually drove value.

real_qa.q: How should brands adapt their strategy for indexing and visibility in an LLM-driven search environment?
real_qa.r: Brands must win on two fronts: first, ensuring they are properly indexed and named in LLM responses so they exist among the options; second, building trust and familiarity so that when LLMs display multiple options, users select the brand they know best. This requires focusing on SEO to be indexed by LLMs while simultaneously building top-of-mind awareness through brand attention metrics, not just immediate conversion.
real_qa.requete: brand strategy LLM indexing top of mind

real_qa.q: According to Jounce reports cited at their summit, what was the reduction in programmatic spend directed to MFA sites between recent years and 2026?
real_qa.r: Mike references Jounce data showing that MFA sites previously captured up to 25 percent of programmatic spend, but by the Jounce Summit in 2026, that figure dropped to underneath 5 percent, possibly even 3 percent, indicating significant industry progress in reducing spend to made-for-advertising sites.

guest.bio_context: Fabien Magonot is CEO and co-founder of Xplain, a company that measures attention generated by advertising across digital channels including open web, social, YouTube, and CTV. He has worked on the publisher side for many years before founding Xplain and brings deep expertise in programmatic advertising and publisher monetization strategies.

real_quote: If everything is labeled as good quality just because it's been on screen for one second, then why not putting 20 ads on screen for one second?
key_stats: Open web impression share declined by 10 points over last couple of years across Xplain client base
MFA programmatic spend reduced from approximately 25% to underneath 5% (possibly 3%) by Jounce Summit 2026
CPC/CPCV pricing is 1.5 to 2 times more expensive than raw CPM for guaranteed outcomes
Average brand requires 8 touchpoints per conversion for a 100-dollar card purchase
Viewability metric was invented 20 years ago to identify ads literally not displayed on screen
